$schema_note: Canonical roster. lib/holdings.js and scripts/make_pdf.py both read this; edit here only.
book_changes_note: Every change to what the book holds, its weights or the method that turns them into an index. Entries before 2026-10-14 are reconstructed from the repository history. Add a line here with every future change; the published page and the PDF render this list.

book_changes.change: Book rebuilt as 18 positions in three buckets (Energy 38 / Compute 32 / Ballast 30), equal weight within each bucket. Added NBIS, CRWV, AMD, TSM, VGT, RARA11.SA, GLD and JPM; dropped a privately marked holding; replaced a dated gold future with GLD.
book_changes.why: Every line publicly priced; spot-backed gold shares remove the roll and expiry.

book_changes.change: Index switched from weight × price to compounded weight-averaged daily returns; series switched to dividend-adjusted (total-return) closes.
book_changes.why: The price-weighted version let a $400 GLD share outvote a $5 KOSPI point regardless of weight; price-only closes read a T-bill fund as flat.

book_changes.change: SGOV and XLP added to Ballast at 5% each; GLD, AVDV, JPM and RARA11.SA cut to 5% so Ballast stayed at 30% (18 → 20 positions).
book_changes.why: The factor test showed Ballast still moving with the thesis. XLP rose 7.5% in the book's worst stretch (2 Jun – 29 Jul 2026); SGOV has had no meaningful drawdown.

book_changes.change: RARA11.SA moved from Ballast to a new Materials bucket (5%); Ballast now 25%.
book_changes.why: A rare-earth basket falls with the book rather than against it, so it was never ballast.
Every line must be investable. The KOSPI is kept as EWY's reference index.

book_changes.change: Headline rebalanced monthly instead of daily; volatility annualised at each series' own observation frequency.
book_changes.why: Daily rebalancing harvests a premium no real book collects at zero cost; the union-calendar curve has ~309 observations a year, not 252.

book_changes.change: Bars keyed by each exchange's own trading date; hedge carry from dated USD and BRL rates; three-factor, three-year regressions on excess returns.
book_changes.why: FX bars arrive stamped the day before, so every non-USD close had been converted at the next day's rate; an independent recomputation of PETR4.SA found it.

book_changes.change: Substrate (renamed from Energy) 42: adds ETN 2 and HUBB 2. Compute 34: adds ASML 2. Materials 2: RARA11.SA 5 -> 2. Ballast 22: AVDV 5 -> 4, JPM 5 -> 4, IEUR 4 added, XLP removed.
book_changes.why: Grid equipment is the bottleneck the thesis names, so it belongs in the bucket beside fuel and land; ASML is the one supplier every fab depends on. IEUR (MSCI Europe) replaces XLP as Ballast's equity line, chosen over EXSA for its lower ASML weight. RARA11 is cut to an option-sized line.
book_changes.breaks: Removed to fund the grid-equipment and European lines. What breaks it: a rotation out of AI into defensives, which XLP caught in the book's worst stretch (+7.5%, 2 Jun - 29 Jul 2026), now lands only on SGOV and GLD, and Ballast loses its one equity line that rose while the thesis fell.

thesis.variant_view: The market prices the AI buildout as a semiconductor story and treats power as a utility input that will be supplied on demand. This book's view is that grid interconnection, fuel and sited land are the binding constraint for the next three to five years, so the scarce rent accrues to whoever owns power, fuel and land with grid access rather than to the designers of the chips; the consensus reprices that only once announced data-centre capacity visibly slips.
thesis.horizon: Three to five years, matching transformer, switchgear and interconnection-queue lead times. Daily and monthly moves are monitored, not acted on.
thesis.review_rules: Reviewed each quarter against the portfolio falsifiers below and every line's own 'what breaks it'. A line is cut when its falsification condition is met, not on price alone; a line whose valuation breaches its bucket's trim rule is cut back to target. If two portfolio falsifiers trigger in the same quarter, the thesis itself is reconsidered, not just the lines.

falsifiers.name: Hyperscaler capex cut
falsifiers.test: Two or more of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta cut next-year capital spending guidance in the same quarter.

falsifiers.name: Compute keeps leading power
falsifiers.test: Compute out-returns Substrate by more than 20 percentage points over twelve months.

falsifiers.name: Uranium price breaks
falsifiers.test: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (a holder of physical uranium) falls more than 25% over twelve months.

falsifiers.name: Memory pricing rolls over
falsifiers.test: Micron, the listed read on HBM pricing, trades more than 30% below its twelve-month high.

falsifiers.name: Oil floor gives way
falsifiers.test: Brent trades below $60, the level at which Saudi Aramco and Petrobras payouts come under pressure.

concentration_groups.name: Taiwan
concentration_groups.why: A Taiwan Strait event is an impairment, not a drawdown; nearly every accelerator in the book is fabricated by TSM, so AMD and the tech funds depend on it too.

concentration_groups.name: Korea memory
concentration_groups.why: HBM supply runs through two Korean makers; the same strait scenario tightens export controls on them.

concentration_groups.name: US AI capex
concentration_groups.why: These lines are paid out of hyperscaler capital spending; one guidance cut moves all of them.

concentration_groups.name: Nuclear fuel
concentration_groups.why: Two funds on one fuel cycle; a reactor incident or a supply restart hits both.

rebalance.note: The headline curve rebalances to target weight on the first session of each month. Daily rebalancing and buy-and-hold are shown beside it for comparison.

cost_assumptions.note: Stated assumptions for the net-of-cost series, not quotes. trade_bps is commission plus half the bid-ask spread per dollar traded, by listing currency. fx_spread_bps is charged on every dollar traded in a non-USD line. withholding_pct is charged on each distribution as if held by a non-US individual investor without treaty relief; interest-related dividends from US T-bill funds can be exempt in practice, so SGOV's drag is overstated, and Brazilian JCP (15%) is ignored. Fund expense ratios are already inside fund prices and are not charged again.

fx_hedge.note: Policy rates used to model a rolled FX hedge back to USD. Held flat across the window; they stand in for forward points, so cross-currency basis and onshore/offshore gaps are ignored. Update with the as_of date when a central bank moves.

positions.name: Global X Uranium ETF
positions.factor_role: The purest listed claim on the fuel bottleneck. Holds miners and enrichers, so it captures the spot uranium move with equity beta stacked on top.
positions.falsification_metric: A restart of idled Kazakh and Namibian supply, or one high-profile reactor incident, resets sentiment far faster than mine supply can respond.

memo.name: Global X Uranium ETF
memo.rationale: Nuclear is the fastest-permitting large-scale answer to hyperscaler 24/7 power demand; the broadest, most liquid way to hold exposure to the fuel cycle.

positions.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
positions.factor_role: Deliberately the boring half of the fuel pair. Weighted toward utilities and reactor builders rather than juniors, it earns cash while URA takes the risk.
positions.falsification_metric: It is not really a uranium proxy — the utility weighting means it can drift with rates while the actual fuel thesis plays out.

memo.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
memo.rationale: Deliberate overlap with URA on the nuclear theme rather than diversifying away from it: the book accepts that thematic concentration, at an ordinary 5% line, in exchange for broader coverage across the fuel cycle and regulated utilities.

positions.name: Petrobras PN
positions.factor_role: Pre-salt barrels at a single-digit multiple with a double-digit payout. Priced for permanent political risk, which is a real risk that is nonetheless already in the number.
positions.falsification_metric: Dividend policy is set by the controlling shareholder, and the controlling shareholder is the state. Fuel-price intervention ahead of an election ends the thesis without warning.

memo.name: Petrobras
memo.rationale: A large, cash-generative conventional producer as a hedge against nuclear permitting delays: thermal generation remains the marginal supplier during interim grid deficits.

positions.name: Saudi Aramco
positions.factor_role: The lowest-cost barrel on earth and the swing producer that sets the floor. Owned as the stabiliser of the bucket, not for its growth.
positions.falsification_metric: Free float is thin and the payout leans on the state budget. A sustained sub-$60 Brent forces a choice between the dividend and Vision 2030.

memo.name: Saudi Aramco
memo.rationale: Same logic as PETR4.SA with a different sovereign and cost-curve position; diversifies the conventional-energy leg across geography rather than concentrating it in one producer.

positions.name: LandBridge Company
positions.factor_role: The hinge of the thesis, held at an ordinary 5% line because a small float makes it one of the book's most fragile names. Owns Permian surface acreage and collects royalties on whatever sits on it — water handling, pipelines, and now data-centre leases. Sells energy and compute demand without drilling or buying a GPU.
positions.falsification_metric: Small float, and the data-centre revenue is a handful of contracts. Concentration cuts both ways: it fell 9.5% in a single session on 12 Aug 2026.

memo.name: LandBridge Company
memo.rationale: Surface and water rights exposure in the Permian Basin: a direct read on interconnection-queue monetization and data-centre land-siting, the physical layer underneath the generation names.

positions.name: Nebius Group
positions.factor_role: A neocloud: rents GPU capacity by the hour to firms that will not build their own. Sits in this bucket because the binding constraint on the business is contracted power and shell space, not chips.
positions.falsification_metric: Capex-funded, customer-concentrated, and competing with hyperscalers who own their own silicon.

memo.name: Nebius Group
memo.rationale: Nebius is a compute landlord: capex-funded, customer-concentrated, and competing with the hyperscalers it sells to. Its unit economics are gated by power access and shell space, not by chips.

positions.name: CoreWeave
positions.factor_role: The scaled version of the same trade as NBIS, with a contracted backlog rather than a spot book. The clearest listed read on whether AI capacity is genuinely pre-sold.
positions.falsification_metric: Debt-funded purchases of an asset that depreciates on a chip cycle. One anchor customer renegotiating resets the whole model, and it overlaps heavily with NBIS — this is one position expressed twice.

memo.name: CoreWeave
memo.rationale: The two neoclouds overlap enough operationally that this is closer to one position expressed twice than two independent bets (see Section 4).

positions.name: Eaton Corporation
positions.factor_role: Switchgear, transformers and power-distribution equipment: the grid hardware whose lead times set how fast new data-centre capacity can be energised.
positions.falsification_metric: Lead times normalise. If transformer and switchgear backlogs shrink as capacity is added, pricing power goes with them, and a multiple built on scarcity re-rates to an industrial one.

memo.name: Eaton Corporation
memo.rationale: Owns the electrical equipment layer between the grid and the rack. Its order backlog and lead-time guidance are the most direct listed read on whether the interconnect bottleneck is binding.

positions.name: Hubbell Incorporated
positions.factor_role: Utility transmission and distribution components: the poles-and-wires hardware utilities need to connect new load.
positions.falsification_metric: Utility capex disappoints. Hubbell sells to utilities, not to data centres, so a pause in rate-base growth or a regulatory squeeze on spending hits it before any AI demand shows up.

memo.name: Hubbell Incorporated
memo.rationale: The utility side of the same bottleneck as Eaton: connecting new load needs transmission and distribution hardware that utilities buy, and that is where its revenue sits.

positions.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
positions.factor_role: The actual bottleneck. Nearly every accelerator in this book is fabricated by one company, so this is the least substitutable position in the portfolio.
positions.falsification_metric: A Taiwan Strait event is not a drawdown, it is a permanent impairment — and the same event takes ^KS11 and 2357.TW with it. The single largest correlated risk here.

memo.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
memo.rationale: The central foundry bottleneck and the counterweight the thesis has to survive: near-monopoly on advanced-node and CoWoS packaging capacity captures the demand growth directly if the rotation thesis is wrong or early.

positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.factor_role: The only credible second source of accelerators. Owned as the option on buyers refusing to accept a single supplier, not as a bet on it winning outright.
positions.falsification_metric: The moat is software, not silicon. If CUDA holds, competitive hardware still does not convert into share, and the share gains are already in the multiple.

memo.name: Advanced Micro Devices
memo.rationale: Second-source accelerator exposure, held at the same weight as its bucket peers rather than sized as a conviction bet: this bucket is insurance against the thesis, not a parallel thesis of its own.

positions.name: Palantir Technologies
positions.factor_role: The application layer. Sells the deployment of models into government and commercial workflows, which is where the margin sits once inference is a commodity.
positions.falsification_metric: The multiple is the position. Growth is real and accelerating, but at this valuation a single decelerating quarter costs more than the growth adds.

memo.name: Palantir Technologies
memo.rationale: Software/deployment-layer exposure, included so the bucket is not pure hardware and does not miss the demand side entirely.

positions.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
positions.factor_role: Broad exposure to the complex, so the bucket survives being wrong about any single name.
positions.falsification_metric: It already holds AMD, TSM's peers and the megacaps, so it overlaps with half this bucket. It dilutes single-name risk without adding a new bet — closer to a cash proxy with tech beta than genuine diversification.

memo.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
memo.rationale: A broad, low-conviction sleeve that keeps the bucket from being a handful of single-name bets on a theme this book is intentionally underweighting.

positions.name: ASUSTeK Computer
positions.factor_role: AI server exposure at a hardware multiple rather than a semiconductor one. The AI server business is repricing the whole company while it is still classified as a PC maker.
positions.falsification_metric: Server assembly is margin-thin with real customer concentration, and the legacy PC cycle still swamps the AI line in reported revenue.

memo.name: ASUSTeK Computer
memo.rationale: Server assembly exposure: margin-thin and customer-concentrated, and the legacy PC cycle still outweighs the AI server line in reported revenue. Held as a read on physical assembly capacity, not a pure AI-server bet.

positions.name: KOSPI Composite
positions.factor_role: Country-level exposure to memory. HBM pricing runs through Korean national accounts, and the index carries a persistent governance discount that is finally being addressed.
positions.falsification_metric: Not directly investable — it is an index, so a real book expresses it through a fund or futures and eats tracking error and FX.

investable.tracking_notes: MSCI Korea 25/50 caps single names, so Samsung and SK Hynix are held below their KOSPI weight; EWY also trades in New York hours against a Seoul close, and carries a 0.59% expense ratio.

positions.substitution_reason: Every line in the book must be investable. The index stays as the reference EWY is measured against.

memo.name: KOSPI Composite Index
memo.rationale: An index proxy for Korea's memory manufacturing exposure to the buildout, avoiding having to pick between the two dominant memory makers.

positions.name: iShares MSCI South Korea ETF
positions.factor_role: Country-level exposure to memory, held through the MSCI Korea fund. HBM pricing runs through Korean national accounts, and the market carries a persistent governance discount that is finally being addressed.
positions.falsification_metric: It is not the KOSPI: MSCI's 25/50 caps hold Samsung and SK Hynix below their index weight, and the fund trades in New York hours against a Seoul close, so a year can open a double-digit gap to the Korean market in either direction.

investable.tracking_notes: MSCI Korea 25/50 caps single names, so Samsung and SK Hynix are held below their KOSPI weight; EWY also trades in New York hours against a Seoul close, and carries a 0.59% expense ratio.

memo.name: iShares MSCI South Korea ETF
memo.rationale: Korea's memory manufacturing exposure to the buildout, held through the country fund rather than by picking between the two dominant memory makers. It replaced the KOSPI index itself on 14 October 2026 so that every line in the book can actually be bought.

positions.name: iShares AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF
positions.factor_role: Spreads the infrastructure bet across semis, cloud and networking, including names the single-name lines here miss.
positions.falsification_metric: Overlaps with VGT and with the megacap complex most portfolios already own, and the LSE line quotes GBP against a USD NAV — an FX layer sitting on top of the actual exposure.

memo.name: AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF (LSE)
memo.rationale: A packaged, diversified sleeve of infrastructure and connectivity names as a lower-maintenance complement to the single-name bets elsewhere in the bucket.

positions.name: ASML Holding (ADR)
positions.factor_role: Sole supplier of EUV lithography: every leading-edge fab in this book depends on its tools.
positions.falsification_metric: Export controls widen. China is a large share of its sales, and a tighter Dutch or US licence regime cuts revenue at once; a foundry capex pause defers orders the multiple assumes.

memo.name: ASML Holding
memo.rationale: The single point every advanced fab passes through. Held small because its fate is tied to the same foundry capex cycle as TSM, and the European index line already carries some of it.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.factor_role: The hedge against the financing of everything above. If the buildout is funded by deficits and suppressed real rates, gold is the direct expression of that — and as spot-backed shares it carries no expiry and no roll.
positions.falsification_metric: Pays nothing to hold. A genuine real-rate spike is its enemy, and it can fall alongside risk assets in a liquidity event precisely when the hedge is needed.

memo.name: SPDR Gold Shares
memo.rationale: Classic drawdown hedge, uncorrelated to the CapEx cycle either way. Held to reduce portfolio volatility, not to express a view.

positions.name: Avantis International Small Cap Value ETF
positions.factor_role: The deliberate opposite of the rest of the book: ex-US, small, cheap, profitable, and largely unowned by the AI trade. Here to be uncorrelated, not to be exciting.
positions.falsification_metric: Value has underperformed growth for most of a decade. If the buildout simply keeps compounding, this is a permanent drag.

memo.name: Avantis Intl Small Cap Value ETF
memo.rationale: Deliberately away from the AI theme entirely: developed-market, value-tilted, small-cap exposure as a genuine diversifier rather than a disguised extra bet on the same trade.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.factor_role: The lender to the buildout. Captures capital-markets activity and a steeper curve without taking a view on which operator wins.
positions.falsification_metric: Imperfect ballast: it is levered to the same economy the rest of the book needs, so it fails in the scenario the hedge exists for. A credit cycle hits it and the neoclouds together.

memo.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
memo.rationale: A quality financial with real exposure to the debt financing the CapEx cycle runs on. Flagged as credit beta rather than ballast: it is levered to the same economy the rest of the book needs, and the risk table shows it diversifies through low correlation, not through a negative one.

positions.name: Investo MVIS Global Rare Earth & Strategic Metals
positions.factor_role: The materials upstream of everything else here: magnets, motors, turbines. Exposure to export controls on rare earths, which is the supply chokepoint the compute bucket cannot design around.
positions.falsification_metric: At 2% it is a sized option on export controls, not a bucket. It breaks if rare-earth export controls ease or Western supply (MP Materials, Lynas) closes the gap, and it can still fall with the rest of the book: a thin, policy-driven BRL listing carrying currency risk on top.

memo.name: Rare Earths / Critical Minerals ETF
memo.rationale: Held in its own Materials bucket rather than in Ballast: a concentrated, policy-driven basket that tracks the same technology-materials cycle as the rest of the book, so in most states it falls with the book rather than against it. The exception is an export-control shock, where it is the one line in the book that re-rates upward. It also traded in only about {coverage} of the measured window, which limits how much its long-horizon return figures should be trusted.

positions.name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
positions.factor_role: US Treasury bills maturing within three months: the closest listed thing to cash that earns the policy rate. It does not rise when AI falls; it simply does not fall, and it is intact and liquid when everything else is not.
positions.falsification_metric: Deep Fed cuts shrink the yield toward zero, and inflation above the yield erodes it in real terms. A US debt-ceiling standoff is the one event that can briefly dent bills themselves.

memo.name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
memo.rationale: Added after the factor test showed the Ballast still moving with the thesis. Treasury bills carry no equity beta and no AI exposure: dry powder that pays the policy rate while the rest of the book is marked down.

positions.name: iShares Core MSCI Europe ETF
positions.factor_role: Broad European equity (MSCI Europe IMI, ~1,000 names): a market whose return does not run through US AI capex.
positions.falsification_metric: It is still equity: it falls with global markets in a broad sell-off, and its largest holding is ASML (4.34% on 13 Oct 2026), a direct link back to the semiconductor cycle the thesis is long.

memo.name: iShares Core MSCI Europe ETF
memo.rationale: Chosen over the STOXX Europe 600 fund (EXSA) because it holds less ASML: 4.34% against 4.41% in the issuer's holdings files for 13 Oct 2026. It tracks MSCI Europe IMI, not the STOXX index.

positions.name: State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF
positions.factor_role: The S&P 500's consumer-staples companies: food, drinks, household goods and the retailers that sell them. Demand for toothpaste does not depend on data-centre capex, and money leaving AI has historically rotated here.
positions.falsification_metric: Still equity: it fell 24.5% in the 2020 crash. Walmart and Costco are a fifth of the fund, tobacco a tenth, and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are a slow threat to food and beverage volumes.

memo.name: State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF
memo.rationale: The defensive-equity leg the Ballast was missing. Over the past year it carried a slightly negative correlation with the Energy and Compute buckets, and it rose while they fell in the book's worst stretch.

positions.removal_note: Removed to fund the grid-equipment and European lines. What breaks it: a rotation out of AI into defensives, which XLP caught in the book's worst stretch (+7.5%, 2 Jun - 29 Jul 2026), now lands only on SGOV and GLD, and Ballast loses its one equity line that rose while the thesis fell.
